title: Initiative Choreography: Quarterly Playbook for Hosted API + Model Catalog
creator: Aisha Barnes
description:
Problem statement: As the hosted API expands our curated model catalog, teams are struggling to coordinate quarterly rollouts, canary bands, and model deprecations without ad-hoc meetings and fragmented guardrails. This ticket captures a repeatable playbook ("initiative choreography") to orchestrate planning, decisioning, and execution for the next quarterly runway so PMs, Eng, Design, and SREs can run predictable, low-risk launches and capacity changes.

Scope: The playbook covers three pillars: 1) Quarterly decision calendar (milestones + review gates), 2) Canary and rollback bands for hosted endpoints and model variants, 3) Model-catalog lifecycle actions (onboard, promote, deprecate, archive) with explicit success thresholds.

Objectives:
- Reduce cross-team coordination overhead for release decisions by 40% (measured by number of ad-hoc syncs).
- Keep hosted-model regression risk below threshold (automated eval pass rate >= 95% on critical prompt set).
- Maintain unit cost targets for 1-2B token workloads (target cost per 1k tokens <= $0.015 for optimized variants).

Deliverables:
- A single-page decision calendar template with dates for: model freeze, eval window, canary start/end, SLA review, deprecation notice.
- Canary playbook with staged traffic bands, metrics to watch, and automated rollback triggers.
- Model Catalog lifecycle checklist (onboarding checklist, risk scorecard, compatibility matrix for fallbacks).
- Runbook snippets for rapid downgrade/fallback to alternate model variants and region routing.

Stakeholders: PM (Aisha Barnes), Eng leads (Liam Chen, Priya Nair), Design lead (Marco Silva), SRE (Elena Ortiz), Applied ML (Jordan Park).
acceptance_criteria: Decision calendar template exists in Confluence and is populated for next quarter
Canary playbook documented with traffic bands, three automated rollback triggers, and owners
Model lifecycle checklist integrated into onboarding flow and model catalog UI work item backlog
At least two cross-functional dry runs completed and feedback captured in retrospective notes

risks: Automated eval infra may not scale for full audit window - mitigation: stagger evals and prioritize critical prompts
SRE capacity constraints during simultaneous canaries - mitigation: limit concurrent canaries per region and pre-book on-call slots
Model quality regressions discovered late in the window - mitigation: tighten pre-canary eval threshold and require sign-off for exception cases
